title: The Part and the Whole
english: And 'the part' is used throughout. So also here, when there is no longer a need for the drinking of 'water' by the Savior 'having given drink' and having made in the 'drinking vessel' 'streams of living water' (John 4:14), the one having in himself the 'spring of living water' does not need 'water'. Therefore he 'crushes' according to it.

And he does not 'crush' somewhere outside, nor does he 'crush' by throwing [it] outside, but... the 'part' is merged with the whole by the 'spring'... that is, the 'annulling' of them and the 'crushing of the water', so that 'water' is no longer needed. Likewise, the intelligible things use words according to names and realities. For since the memory of a 'spring' is... 'crushed' 'the part' and... concerning perfect knowledge... 'crushing' of 'water'... 'annulment of the part'... the text: 'the part' and the 'water' are the same, and the 'spring' [is the same].
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Wheel upon the Pit
english: And what is the 'face to face'? We often encounter this, where the presence 'abolishes the partial'. Often we say that [something] is more pleasant for one to hear, from which we would be benefited if we see him; there we 'crush' those things, because we perceive greater [things], we 'cast out' them; we do not set them aside, but rather we 'crush' them into greater [things].

12,6d And so the wheel shall run upon the pit (Ecclesiastes 12:6). It is possible to draw from a parallel 'pit'; just as it is to draw 'water' from a 'spring', so also to draw water from a 'pit' with a 'wheel'. When therefore there is no longer a need to move [it] thus, then 'the wheel shall run upon the pit' and destroys it. And it is also possible otherwise; for each verse is a line, and each line has its own meaning. We say therefore this, that in many...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Pit and the Helplessness of Christ
english: In the places of Scripture, Hades is named the 'pit'. For see what it says: 'Lord, you brought my soul up from Hades, you saved me from those descending into the pit' (Psalm 130:7). And the Savior, having become man and having accepted death on behalf of men, says: 'I was numbered among those descending into the pit, since I became as a helpless man'. He was crucified and his hands and his feet were as 'helpless'; 'he was heard like a sheep toward slaughter' (Isaiah 53:7), as 'helpless'. And he led himself into the 'helplessness'. And he brings forward: 'free among the dead', and 'I was numbered among those descending into the pit', and 'helpless man' it seemed to be, but 'free among the dead' I am. And one is able to understand 'free among the dead', that is, without sin.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
